picks.title: Welcome + Opening Remarks

speakers.bio: Jonathan Bryce is the Executive Director of Cloud & Infrastructure at the Linux Foundation, where he leads both the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and the OpenInfra Foundation—two of the largest and most influential open source communities in the world. With over 15 years of open source leadership, Jonathan co-founded the OpenStack project, guiding its evolution into a global ecosystem that supports a multi-billion-dollar market and serves as the de facto standard for open cloud infrastructure. Before his open source career, Jonathan spent over a decade in data center infrastructure and co-founded one of the industry’s earliest cloud computing companies, which grew into a billion-dollar business following its acquisition by Rackspace. Passionate about open collaboration, infrastructure innovation, and empowering users, contributors, and ecosystems worldwide, Jonathan frequently speaks at international conferences on open source strategy, infrastructure modernization, cloud-native technologies, and open source AI initiatives.

speakers.tagLine: building a better world through open collaboration
speakers.bio: building a better world through open collaboration

Robert Nishihara is one of the creators of Ray, the world’s leading open source AI compute engine. Ray is used by companies across the board from Canva to Runway to Coinbase to Pinterest to scale their machine learning training, inference, and data processing workloads. He is one of the co-founders of Anyscale, which is the company behind Ray. He did his PhD in machine learning and distributed systems in the computer science department at UC Berkeley. Before that, he majored in math at Harvard.

speakers.tagLine: Principal software engineer, Kubernetes AI Conformance program chair and sig-auth chair
speakers.bio: Rita Zhang is a Principal software engineer at CoreWeave, based in San Francisco bay area. She works on the inference platform powering the serverless and dedicated inference products. She is a Kubernetes sig-auth chair, a Kubernetes AI Conformance program chair, and a maintainer of the Open policy agent Gatekeeper project. Rita is passionate about open source and running distributed workloads at scale.

Kevin Cochrane is a 25+ year pioneer of the digital experience space. Kevin co-founded his first start-up, Interwoven, in 1996, pioneered open source content management at Alfresco in 2006, and built a global leader in digital experience management as CMO of Day Software and later Adobe. Kevin has also held senior executive positions at OpenText, Bloomreach, and SAP. Now at Vultr, Kevin is working to build Vultr's global brand presence as a leader in the independent cloud platform market.

speakers.tagLine: Crossplane Steering Committee, Founder & CEO Upbound
speakers.bio: Bassam has created two CNCF-graduated open source projects, Crossplane and Rook, and now leads Modelplane, an open source control plane for AI inference. He is a founding member of the Crossplane Steering Committee, and the CEO & Founder of Upbound, the control plane company.

speakers.tagLine: Let's keep the modern world running, sustainably.

Jorge O. Castro is a community engineer, specializing in Open Source. He's basically a cat herder – a combination of engineering, developer relations, and user advocacy. 

These days Jorge is the Technical Program Management Director at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, where he's tasked with helping make open source sustainable. He has worked on Ubuntu, Kubernetes, Kubeflow, Cloud Custodian, and Project Bluefin.

picks.title: Kubeflow Graduation: Powering the Next Era of Cloud Native AI With an Open Community

speakers.bio: Ron Kahn is a Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA, a maintainer of NVIDIA Grove project, and snapshot project. When not simplifying AI for Kubernetes, Ron can be found cooking something delicious.

Andrey Velichkevich is an AI Engineer at Apple and a key contributor to the Kubeflow and Kubernetes projects. He serves on the Kubeflow Steering Committee and is a co-chair for Kubernetes WG WAS and Checkpoint/Restore. In addition, Andrey is an active member of the Batch WG, SIG Scheduling, and the CNCF AI TSG. He is a co-author of the CNCF AI White Paper and actively contributes to multiple AI initiatives that advance the CNCF community and the broader cloud-native AI ecosystem.

speakers.tagLine: AWS, Principal Technologist, OSS - Data, AI and Kubernetes
speakers.bio: Vara Bonthu is a Principal Technologist at AWS and CNCF maintainer for the Kubeflow Spark Operator and MCP Server for Spark History Server. He leads the Data-on-EKS and AI-on-EKS open-source initiatives and has operated Spark on Kubernetes at the scale of thousands of nodes and hundreds of thousands of pods. His work focuses on performance, resiliency, and AI-driven observability for Spark, Ray, and Kubeflow.

Ekin is a Developer Advocate at NVIDIA, following the acquisition of Run:ai. Prior to that, she specialized in the privacy implications of federated learning systems with DNNs. Currently, she is exploring the efficient usage of large models in production and one of the maintainers of KAI scheduler, which is a CNCF sandbox project.

Manabu is a Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services. He focuses on contributing to open source application delivery tooling and works with AWS strategic customers to design and implement enterprise solutions using AWS resources and open source technologies. His interests include Kubernetes, GitOps, Serverless, and Souls Series.

picks.title: Cloud Native Without Limits: What Can AI Agents Do for Us?

speakers.bio: Lin is the Head of Open Source at Solo.io, contributing full-time to the open-source community. She serves on the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), is a CNCF Ambassador, and is a maintainer for Istio, kgateway, and kagent. An international speaker at tech conferences, Lin frequently blogs about gateways, service meshes, cloud-native connectivity, and AI agents. She is the author of “Sidecar-less Istio Explained” and “AI Agents in Kubernetes”, and holds more than 200 patents.
